name: grill-me
description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding. Walk down every branch of the decision tree, resolving dependencies between decisions one-by-one.

name: grilling
description: The grilling engine: interview the user in rounds across the frontier of undecided questions, each with a recommended answer, until nothing is left silently assumed. Installed automatically as a dependency of grill-me and grill-with-docs.

name: grill-with-docs
description: Domain-aware grilling that checks existing documentation, enforces terminology, cross-references code, and updates CONTEXT.md and ADRs inline during the interview

name: domain-modeling
description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model: challenge terminology, write GLOSSARY.md, and record ADRs while designing. Installed automatically as a dependency of grill-with-docs.

name: ponytail
description: Forces the laziest solution that actually works. YAGNI, stdlib first, native platform features before dependencies. Active every response — zero over-engineering.

name: ponytail-review
description: Review a diff for over-engineering. Finds what to delete: reinvented stdlib, needless deps, speculative abstractions. One line per finding. Invoke manually: /ponytail-review.

name: logan
description: Opinionated frontend architecture mentor persona. Use for: frontend/React/TypeScript design decisions, code review, proposing or challenging solutions, debugging errors/exceptions/test failures with root-cause teaching, state management architecture, component structure, hooks, reusability, refactoring, anti-pattern detection. Applies Hook-View-Controller separation, Bunshi/molecule-style dependency injection, and higher-order reusable utilities. Brutally honest reviews, professor-style deep explanations, challenges weak solutions, always current with MDN and modern web platform features. Supports "logan off" override for direct answers. Invoke for any frontend solution design, PR review, error, or "how should I build this" question.

name: vue-reviewer
description: Opinionated Vue and TypeScript architecture mentor and code reviewer. Use for: Vue SFC design, Composition API, script setup, composables, reactivity bugs, props/emits/slots/v-model APIs, provide/inject, Pinia or shared-state decisions, component-library work, CSS Modules, design tokens, accessibility, Storybook/Vitest tests, migrations from Vue 2 or Options API, PR review, debugging, refactoring, and "how should I build this" questions. Applies contract-first component APIs, computed-over-synchronized-state, narrow state ownership, repository-aware modern-vs-legacy rules, behavior-matrix testing, and backwards-compatible library design. Direct, evidence-driven, mentor-style, and current with official Vue guidance. Supports "vue-reviewer off" override for direct answers.

name: slopsift
description: Lint prose with the SlopSift CLI and interpret its structural AI-writing findings without guessing authorship. Use when reviewing or editing Markdown, documentation, website copy, release notes, plain text, or source-code comments for canned arguments, vague attribution, unsupported certainty, repetitive structure, AI vocabulary, and related writing tells.
